plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of pea-like flowers hang from twisting woody vines and drape fences, pergolas and walls in soft purple. In many gardens the display arrives just as the new leaves unfold.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late May in cool temperate regions such as southern Ontario, Canada, with occasional repeat blooms through summer
plants.location: Temperate gardens of eastern North America (for example Ontario, Canada), native to China
plants.funFact: Wisteria is a twining vine that can live for decades. Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria twines clockwise.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This is the autumn-flowering camellia. Its glossy evergreen shrubs fill with delicate, open blooms in white, pink and red while the leaves of the surrounding trees turn gold. It is a cheerful sight as the Southern Hemisphere cools into winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: April to June (autumn) in southern Australia
plants.location: Southern Australia, including cool-climate parks and gardens (native to Japan)
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are also pressed for oil in parts of Asia.

plants.name: Rhododendron ponticum
plants.description: This vigorous evergreen shrub forms dense thickets covered in rounded clusters of bell-shaped flowers. Each bloom is flecked with greenish-yellow spots, and the show stands out against dark, leathery leaves.
plants.location: Black Sea region (Turkey and Georgia), Iberia and many gardens across temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Its nectar can make honey toxic, and the plant has a long history of causing 'mad honey' poisoning around the Black Sea. It has also become a problematic invader in the British Isles.
